title: Build a feature, to its pull request

tasks.title: The feature specification
tasks.text: write the specification of the feature this request describes, docs/product/specs/<feature>.md. The feature's name, and so the file, come from the request. Every requirement carries where it came from and every judgment word a number. Ask the person what only they can answer and never invent a requirement; the specification is ready when its Readiness line says `Ready for architecture: yes`, and while a question blocks a requirement, stop and ask it.

tasks.title: The design
tasks.text: the specification is done and ready (docs/product/specs/, the file of the feature). Design the feature: the parts, what each owns, how data flows between them, the contracts that hold, and how each acceptance criterion will be checked. Write docs/engineering/designs/<feature>.md, and a decision record in docs/engineering/adr/ for every decision that could reasonably have gone another way.

tasks.title: The failing unit tests
tasks.text: the specification and the design are done (docs/product/specs/ and docs/engineering/designs/). Write the unit tests of the feature from the specification's requirements, edge cases and acceptance criteria, in the project's own test runner and next to its existing tests. They must fail today for the reason they name, and no source under test changes. Record them, and what each showed before the change, in the Failing tests section of the plan of this task, docs/engineering/plans/<task>.md (a short kebab-case name from the request).

tasks.title: Implement the feature
tasks.text: the failing tests are written (the tests listed in the Failing tests section of the plan docs/engineering/plans/<task>.md) and the design is done (docs/engineering/designs/). There is no backlog task, and the plan is not a fix plan (it has no root cause): work as for a failing check with no task id, the check being the command that section names. Run it before touching any file and quote the failing line, make the smallest change that makes the tests pass without editing them, run the project's fast checks and quote the passing lines. Touch only the files the design names for this feature. Propose the commit and do not make it.

tasks.title: Integration tests
tasks.text: the feature is implemented (the change on the current branch, read as its diff against the base). Show that it works where people meet it, not only in the unit that was edited: write the integration tests the project's runner supports, run them, and make sure each test of new behaviour fails on the code before the change and each test of preserved behaviour passes on it. Record the result in the Integration tests section of the plan.

tasks.title: Review the change
tasks.text: the feature is implemented and tested (docs/engineering/plans/<task>.md). Review the change on the current branch against the specification and the design (docs/product/specs/ and docs/engineering/designs/): run the project's checks, and write the review, docs/engineering/reviews/<change>.md, with only findings a developer can act on (the location, the quoted line, why it fails, how to fix it). Fix nothing in this task.

tasks.title: Update the documentation
tasks.text: the change is reviewed (docs/engineering/reviews/). Update the documents the change made wrong or left without a mention (reference pages, guides, examples, the README), checking every edit by running code, and record each sentence before and after in the Docs section of the plan docs/engineering/plans/<task>.md.

tasks.title: Prepare the pull request
tasks.text: the change is on the current branch, reviewed and documented. Prepare its pull request into the base branch and stop at the confirmation gate: show the payload and ask.
